title: Architecture-aware kernel curation and gradual "seatbelt" rollout for MHA/GQA/MoE builds
creator: Ravi Menon
description:
Goal: build an automated, reviewable pipeline that curates per-model kernel/compile bundles and publishes performance profiles for MHA, GQA, and MoE architectures, then rolls them out gradually with a safety "seatbelt" to prevent regressions.

Background: onboarding new model families currently requires manual kernel picks and ad-hoc performance checks. For complex architectures (Mixture-of-Experts, Grouped-Query Attention, and multi-headed attention variants) the optimal kernel set depends on shard layout, sequence length distribution, batch concurrency, and quantization path. We need a repeatable workflow that:
- Generates candidate compile bundles per model variant and runtime target (arch/fp/quant).
- Runs targeted microbenchmarks and representative prompt suites to produce a profile (latency/throughput/95/99, memory usage, token cost).
- Produces a signed profile artifact with metadata (model hash, repo commit, kernel versions, hardware fingerprint).
- Publishes the profile to the model catalog and updates the onboard manifest with an explicit pin.
- Enables a staged rollout that starts on low-risk routes and ramps to production with automatic rollback if telemetry crosses thresholds.

Scope of work:
1) Curator pipeline: new CI stage that enumerates kernel candidates, builds bundles, records deterministic build metadata, and stores artifacts in S3. Uses existing compiler infra but adds an "architecture probe" that samples MoE expert count, GQA group sizes, and MHA head counts to choose candidate kernel variants.
2) Profile runner: harness to execute microbenchmarks (latency p95/p99, cold vs warm KV, memory high-water) and representative prompt evaluations (quality smoke tests). Outputs profile JSON and a human-readable summary.
3) Pin manifest format: extend manifest with fields: profile_version, profile_checksum, kernel_set_id, hardware_fingerprints, validity_window, and deprecation_policy. All values must be immutable once published; replacements create a new profile_version.
4) Seatbelt rollout: a staged deployment controller with policy knobs: initial routes (5% canary on internal customers), ramp schedule, metrics gates (p95 latency increase <= 10ms, error-rate delta <= 0.1%, regression in quality evals <= 2%), automatic rollback window.
5) Telemetry and alerting: new dashboards and composite alerts for profile rollouts, including per-model, per-kernel telemetry. Add alert playbooks for on-call to interpret and rollback.
6) Safety nets: fallback mapping so that when a profile is rejected or runtime detects ABI mismatch it can revert to the last-good profile or a baseline generic bundle.

Acceptance criteria:
- Curator pipeline produces signed profile artifacts for three internal models (demo-mha-v2, demo-gqa-small, demo-moe-8e) and uploads to the catalog.
- Profile runner generates reproducible JSON with key stats and a stable checksum.
- Pin manifest is created and used by the model-onboarder to route new deployments to the curated kernel set.
- Seatbelt rollout executed for demo-gqa-small with automated gates stopping ramp on a synthetic latency regression in canary.
- Documentation: onboarding playbook + step-by-step runbook added to Confluence and linked in the catalog entry.

Open questions / trade-offs to resolve:
- How aggressive should compile specialization be? Deep specialization reduces latency but increases binary size and maintenance surface (we may need a size cap by model family).
- What is the timeline for supporting cross-architecture bundles vs single-arch pins? Supporting multi-arch pins adds complexity to the curator but improves reliability.
- How to version profile metadata without tying release cadence to runtime releases? We should adopt semantic profile versions separate from runtime semver.

Security & compliance notes: built artifacts must be signed by CI and have provenance metadata; treat profile artifacts as first-class configuration (audit logs required).

acceptance_tests: Run curator pipeline for demo-mha-v2, confirm profile_checksum matches recorded value and profile_version is unique.
Execute profile runner suite and verify p95/p99, memory usage, and quality smoke tests pass within thresholds.

implementation_notes: Use existing compiler CI image but add deterministic build flags to ensure reproducible artifacts.
Add a lightweight hardware fingerprinting step that collects architecture, cuda driver version, and cuDNN/onednn versions.
Expose rollout policy via the Console so PMs can schedule ramps and SRE can tune gates without code deploy.
